# LinkedIn Reviews

### The community submitted 79 reviews to tell us what they like about LinkedIn, what LinkedIn can do better, and more.

Based on 79 reviews

Review LinkedIn?

Reviewers largely see LinkedIn as the default place for professional networking, job search, hiring, research, and building a public work profile. Many say it works best when used actively through posting, commenting, and outreach, and several founders credit it with warm intros, early users, and customer conversations; the maker of Extrovert calls it the best place to build sales relationships. The main complaints are repetitive AI-generated content, spammy messages, cluttered feeds, weak filtering, occasional poor job or support experiences, and a shift toward less professional content.

It’s invaluable for connecting with peers, discovering job opportunities, and showcasing expertise through posts, articles, and profile updates. LinkedIn has evolved to support not just job-seekers but also companies and entrepreneurs who want to build their brands, find clients, and engage in industry-relevant conversations. With its strong emphasis on thought leadership and professional growth, LinkedIn is a key tool for anyone aiming to expand their professional reach and influence.

Review LinkedIn?

Reviewers mostly see LinkedIn as the default place for professional networking, job hunting, recruiting, and building a public work profile. Many say it helps them reach recruiters, clients, founders, and decision-makers, and some report real conversations, leads, and hires from posts or search. Makers of Extrovert and Lyto also credit it for relationship-building and early user growth. The main complaints are a cluttered feed, spammy messages, fake profiles, AI-generated fluff, weak filtering, and some poor job or support experiences.
